doc.title: Scott Jimmy — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Herman Lubinsky and Savoy in Newark
summary: Lubinsky invited him in Newark, Freddie Mendelsohn arranged the studio, and again he did not pick material.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: [recording interrupted]
My name is David Ritz, here in the home of Jeannie and Jimmy Scott, September 24th, 2008. I can’t believe it’s 2008. 2008.
How about that.
2008, and you were born in 1925.
Yeah, how about that.
That’s beautiful. You lived a long and one of the most interesting lives of anyone I’ve ever met in my life.
A long time.
I would have to say you have lived one of the most interesting lives of anyone I’ve ever met in my life.
It’s been rough.
Been rough.
But I’ll overcome.

I will overcome, he says. Let’s get back to the timeline here. 1953 you do the things for Roost and this and that. Then, from the middle of the 1950s to the end of the 1950s, you’re in Newark and you’re getting hooked up with this guy named Herman Lubinsky. How did you meet Herman?
He came to meet me at the club that I was at. I was at a club there. He came over and invited me to the store, because he did all this work right above one of the stores that he had.
This is in Newark.
In Newark. Then that’s when he told – what was his name? The one that worked . . .
Freddie Mendelsohn?
Yes. That’s when he told Freddie to arrange the studio. I think that was in Linden, that studio.
Where you began to record. You knew of his recording label, Savoy.
Yeah, but I didn’t know what he was doing to folks.
But you knew that on his label Charlie Parker recorded.
Right. I mean, then he had a big thing with Wynonie Harris. That was his biggest thing. He wanted that back again. But Wynonie Harris was dead and gone.
So he basically saw you as a guy who might be able to give him some hits the way Wynonie Harris had given him some r-and-b.
Yeah, but like I told you yesterday, everything was what he wanted. Nothing was what I wanted to do, which I felt good about doing. That wasn’t the case.
